headline: Aromatase inhibitors
body: work for height in some people and not others

headline: What they do
body: *Letrozole* and *anastrozole* block aromatase. | Less testosterone converts into estradiol. | Estradiol is what drives skeletal maturation, so blocking the conversion slows bone age.
punch: Androgen keeps working. The closing signal drops.

headline: Where it worked
body: Hero 2006. Boys with **constitutional delay of puberty**. | Testosterone plus placebo against testosterone plus letrozole, for 12 months. | Followed all the way to **near final height**, not predicted.

headline: Where it did not
body: Letrozole **monotherapy** in pre and early pubertal boys. | Followed to adult height. | It did not increase it.
punch: Same drug. Different population. Opposite result.

headline: Which tells you
body: This is not a drug that works or does not. | It worked alongside testosterone, in boys who were late, given during adolescence. | It failed alone, in younger boys, given before puberty was underway.
punch: Timing and pairing decide the outcome.

headline: Combination
body: Mauras ran aromatase inhibitor against growth hormone against both together in pubertal boys with idiopathic short stature. | Combination beat either alone over 24 to 36 months. | Which fits the mechanism: GH drives growth while the AI holds the plate open.
punch: Two different levers, not competing ones.

headline: Anastrozole vs letrozole
body: were compared head to head over 3 years in 79 pubertal males. | Letrozole produced higher testosterone, lower estradiol, and **slower bone age advance**. | It also produced slower growth velocity.
punch: Stronger suppression. Slower growth. Same tradeoff as always.

headline: Now the measurement problem
body: A lot of AI studies report **predicted** adult height. | Predicted height is a model output. It is a forecast from a bone age reading, not a measured adult. | Wickman reported a 5.1 cm gain in predicted height.
punch: Predicted and achieved are different endpoints.

headline: So when you read one
body: find out which number they measured. | Near final height means they waited and measured a person. | Predicted adult height means they ran a calculation.

headline: The safety signal
body: Jacobson 2005. 24 adolescent males, 12 months of letrozole. | Bone age progression fell from **1.51 to 0.68**. That part gets quoted. | Then they ran low dose ACTH stimulation testing.
punch: Roughly one in four showed subnormal response.

headline: The authors concluded
body: mild **adrenal suppression**. | Aromatase inhibition is not organ selective. The adrenal participates in steroid synthesis too. | You cannot inhibit an enzyme in only the tissue you aimed at.
punch: They looked and they found something.

headline: And the monitoring gap
body: Paediatric height studies generally do not screen for the sensory and cognitive outcomes that oncology treats as routine for these drugs. | Your brain expresses aromatase and makes estrogen locally. | Blocking the enzyme systemically blocks it there too.
punch: No reported harm is not the same as no harm.

headline: So the honest summary
body: Aromatase inhibitors do increase height in specific contexts, with near final height data behind them. | They fail in others. Population, timing and whether they are paired with androgen all matter. | And the safety monitoring in this population is thinner than in oncology.
punch: Effective in context. Not effective in general.
